title: Chemical pulldown combined with mass spectrometry to identify the molecular targets of antimalarials in cell-free lysates
protocol: Transfer the resin slurry to microcentrifuge tubes.
Add approximately 400 μL of Cytiva NHS activated Sepharose 4 fast flow resin slurry to each tube.
Label one vial ‘high’ loading level and one ‘low’ loading level.
Cap the tube and centrifuge at 15,000 g for 30 seconds at room temperature.
Allow the resin to settle for approximately 1 minute.
Estimate the volume of settled resin using the volume indicators on the side of the microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the resin and allow the surface to settle flat for approximately one minute.
Remove supernatant after settling the surface flat.
Wash the resin with DMSO to remove the 2-propanol storage solvent.
Remove the supernatant with a 200 μL pipette without disturbing the settled resin.
Add 1 mL of molecular biology grade DMSO to the microcentrifuge tube and gently shake to mix.
Centrifuge the tube at 15,000 g for 30 seconds at room temperature.
Carefully remove the supernatant with a 1,000 μL pipette.
Repeat steps 2b and 2c two more times.
After the final washing step, add 200 μL of either DDD02355221 high loading reaction stock solution or DDD02355221 low loading reaction stock solution to appropriately labeled tubes.
Cap the tubes and centrifuge at 15,000 g for 30 seconds at room temperature.
Transfer 10 μL of supernatant from each tube to a separate Agilent screw top vial with fixed insert as t = 0 reading for analysis by HPLC.
Re-cap the tubes and mix well by inverting several times.
Secure the capped tubes inside a 50 mL Falcon tube using cotton wool.
Place the Falcon tube on a MACSmix™ tube rotator.
Rotate at maximum speed setting (20 rpm) for 24 h at room temperature.
Centrifuge the tubes (15,000 g, 30 s, room temperature).
Transfer 10 μL of resulting supernatants from each tube to Agilent screw top vials with fixed insert labeled as t = 24 h “high” and t = 24 h “low”.
Carefully remove the remaining supernatant using a 200 μL pipette.
Add 1 mL of DMSO to each tube.
Cap the tubes and gently shake to mix.
Centrifuge the tubes (15,000 g, 30 s, room temperature).
Remove the supernatant with a 1,000 μL pipette.
Repeat steps 4d and 4e a further two times.
Block the drug beads with ethanolamine by adding 200 μL of 200 mM ethanolamine stock solution to each tube.
Invert and shake the tubes gently to mix the drug beads.
Secure the microcentrifuge tubes using cotton wool inside a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Place on a MACSmix™ tube rotator and rotate at maximum speed setting (20 rpm) at room temperature for 24 h.
Pellet the drug beads by centrifugation (15,000 g, 30 s, room temperature).
Carefully remove the supernatant from each tube with a 200 μL pipette.
Add 1 mL of DMSO to both tubes and gently shake to mix the drug beads.
Centrifuge the tubes (15,000 g, 30 s, room temperature) to pellet the drug beads.
Carefully remove the supernatant with a 1,000 μL pipette.
Repeat steps 5d and 5e two more times.
Transfer drug beads to storage solution by adding 1 mL of 2-propanol to both tubes.
Invert and shake gently to mix the drug beads.
Centrifuge (15,000 g, 30 s, room temperature) and remove the supernatant from each tube with a 1,000 μL pipette.
Repeat steps 6a and 6b two more times.
Estimate the volume of settled drug beads using the volume indicators on the side of the microcentrifuge tubes.
Add 2-propanol to make a 1:1 slurry.
Prepare a 1:1 drug bead to 2-propanol slurry.
Analyze probe attachment on the drug beads (steps 7-11).
Do not proceed with pulldown experiments until probe attachment analysis is completed.
Store drug beads at 4°C if not immediately needed for pulldown experiments.
Perform pulldown experiments as close to synthesis time as possible.
Prepare samples for HPLC analysis to establish efficiency of probe attachment.
Prepare stock solutions for an eight-point standard curve by serial dilution from a 50 mM DMSO stock of DDD02355221.
Pipette 10 μL of each standard curve stock solution (excluding 8-point set) into a low volume HPLC vial.
Dilute with 190 μL of 1:1 MeCN/water and mix.
Independently prepare 10 mM, 1 mM, and 0.1 mM stock solutions of DDD02355221 to serve as quality control samples.
Pipette 10 μL of each validation stock solution into a low volume HPLC vial.
Dilute with 190 μL of 1:1 MeCN/water and mix.
Prepare a fresh 10 mM probe stock solution for quality control samples if possible.
Dilute the t = 0 h and t = 24 h aliquots of high- and low-loading drug beads with 190 μL of 1:1 MeCN/water mixture.
Mix the diluted solutions thoroughly.
Filter the mixed solutions through a 13 mm 0.2 μm syringe filter.
Set up an HPLC method with a flow rate of 0.800 mL min-1 and injection volume of 3 μL.
Perform a pre-equilibration at 95:5 (A:B) for 30 seconds.
Run a linear gradient from 95:5 to 5:95 (A:B) from 0.0 to 2.2 minutes.
Hold the gradient at 5:95 (A:B) from 2.2 to 3.0 minutes.
Return to 95:5 (A:B) flow rate from 3.0 to 4.0 minutes.
Analyze standard curve, quality control, and experimental samples in triplicate using HPLC.
Construct a DDD02355221 standard curve based on the UV chromatogram peak areas.
Calculate the concentration of DDD02355221 in t = 0 h and t = 24 h samples from the standard curve.
Input peak areas for peaks corresponding to the probe in UV chromatograms into the provided excel spreadsheet.
Fill in the aX + bY values from the standard curve equation into the corresponding cells in the excel spreadsheet.
Determine the concentration of quality control samples (10 mM, 1 mM, and 0.1 mM) using the standard curve.
Transfer resin slurry to a microcentrifuge tube.
Wash and resuspend the resin in DMSO.
Add 400 μl of Cytiva NHS-activated Sepharose 4 Fast Flow resin slurry to a 1.5 ml screw cap microcentrifuge tube.
Cap the tube.
Centrifuge at 15,000 g for 30 seconds at room temperature.
Allow to stand for approximately 1 minute to settle.
Carefully remove the supernatant with a 200 μL pipette without disturbing the settled resin.
Add 1 mL of DMSO to the tube.
Cap and invert the tube, gently shaking to mix.
Centrifuge at 15,000 g for 30 seconds at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant carefully with a 1,000 μL pipette.
Repeat steps involving DMSO addition, centrifugation, and removal of supernatant two further times.
Add 200 μL of 200 mM ethanolamine stock solution to the settled resin.
Cap the microcentrifuge tube and invert, shaking gently to mix.
Place the capped microcentrifuge tube on a MACSmix™ tube rotator at maximum rotation (20 rpm) for 24 hours at room temperature.
Centrifuge at 15,000 g for 30 seconds at room temperature after mixing.
Carefully remove the supernatant with a 200 μL pipette.
Add 1 mL of DMSO to the pelleted resin and gently shake to mix.
Centrifuge at 15,000 g for 30 seconds at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant carefully with a 1,000 μL pipette.
Repeat steps involving ethanolamine treatment, centrifugation, removal of supernatant, DMSO addition and mixing, and subsequent centrifugation and supernatant removal two further times.
Add 1 mL of 2-propanol to the blank resin and gently shake to mix.
Centrifuge at 15,000 g for 30 seconds at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant with a 1,000 μL pipette.
Repeat steps involving 2-propanol addition, centrifugation, and removal of supernatant two further times.
Estimate the volume of settled resin using the volume indicators on the side of the microcentrifuge tube.
Add 2-propanol to make a 1:1 slurry with the resin.
Decrease the hematocrit to 2% around 3 days before starting the pulldown experiment.
Transfer approximately 560 mL of culture to a HYPERFlaskTM.
Increase the volume of culture to 375 mL by adding CMM to reduce the hematocrit to 2%.
Add 150 mL of CMM/2% erythrocytes to obtain a volume of 525 mL.
Pour the culture into the HYPERFlaskTM in a steady stream, avoiding bubbles.
Top up with more CMM/2% erythrocytes to ensure the flask is completely full.
Tap the sides of the HYPERFlaskTM firmly by hand to release any air bubbles.
Secure the lid on the HYPERFlaskTM.
Invert the HYPERFlaskTM several times to mix.
Incubate the HYPERFlaskTM at 37°C with 1% O2 and 3% CO2 in a balance of N2.
Refresh media 1 or 2 times per day.
Check parasitemia daily by preparing a thin smear.
Stand the HYPERFlaskTM upright approximately one hour before changing the media.
Aspirate off about one third of the culture volume without disturbing the erythrocytes.
Refill the HYPERFlaskTM with CMM supplemented with 0.4% erythrocytes every second day.
Release air bubbles and mix the culture well.
Proceed with the preparation of the lysate when parasitemia reaches 8-12%.
Pre-chill pellet wash buffer on ice.
Pre-chill saponin solution on ice.
Pre-chill lysis buffer on ice.
Pre-chill Octyl-β-D-glucopyranoside solution on ice.
Rinse cell disruption vessel chamber with lysis buffer.
Chill rinsed vessel on ice.
Stand up HYPERFlaskTM to allow erythrocytes to settle for 1 hour.
Aspirate off about 20% of the media from the top.
Transfer culture to centrifuge tubes.
Pellet cells by centrifugation at 1,800 g and deceleration setting 2 at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Resuspend pelleted cells in 5 pellet volumes of ice-cold saponin solution.
Incubate resuspended cells on ice for 10 minutes with vigorous mixing every 2–3 minutes to lyse erythrocytes.
Centrifuge resuspended cells at 2,800 g and deceleration setting 5 at 4°C for 8 minutes.
Carefully aspirate off the supernatant.
Wash free parasites 3 times with pellet wash buffer.
Aspirate supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 25 mL pellet wash buffer.
Centrifuge resuspended pellet at 2,800 g and deceleration setting 5 at 4°C for 8 minutes.
Repeat twice more.
Supernatant should be a pale straw-colored solution after the final wash.
If the supernatant is still pink, perform an additional wash step.
Resuspend the pellet in 0.5 pellet volumes of lysis buffer.
Mix well to ensure no clumps remain.
Transfer directly to the chamber of the cell disruption vessel.
Add 0.5 pellet volumes of octyl-β-D-glucopyranoside solution.
Close the chamber tightly.
Connect the cell disruption vessel to a nitrogen cylinder.
Adjust pressure to 1,500 psi.
Incubate on ice for 60 min.
Very carefully open the pressure valve.
Release the lysate dropwise into a 50 mL falcon tube.
Incubate the parasite lysate with blank beads.
Incubate the pre-treated lysates with an excess of competitor or DMSO.
Add drug beads to the treated lysates.
Incubate the lysates and beads together.
Wash the beads after incubation.
Vortex the bead slurry.
Transfer 20 μl/sample of each resin sample to a LoBind® Eppendorf tube.
Add 1 ml ddH2O to each resin sample.
Centrifuge the resin samples (10,000 g, 30 s, room temperature).
Remove supernatants from the resin samples with a pipette and discard.
Repeat washing steps twice more substituting ddH2O with lysis buffer containing 0.8 mg/mL Octyl-β-D-glucopyranoside.
Transfer lysate supernatant to a fresh LoBind® tube and keep on ice.
Measure protein content of lysate using Bio-Rad Quick Start™ Bradford kit.
Dilute the provided 2 mg/ml BSA solution to 0.5 mg/ml in ddH2O for standard curve preparation.
Add volumes of diluted BSA solution (0, 1.25, 2.5, 5, 10, 20 μl) to each of six 70 μl cuvettes.
Add 0.5 μl and 1 μl of lysate respectively to two cuvettes for protein measurement.
Add 1 mL Bradford reagent to each cuvette.
Incubate the cuvettes at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Measure the absorbance at 595 nm using a spectrophotometer.
Dilute lysate to 2 mg/mL in lysis buffer.
Incubate lysate with pre-washed blank beads, rotating on a MACSMix™ rotator at 4°C for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge the mixture at 10,000 g for 30 seconds at room temperature.
Remove and discard the supernatant.
Split the remaining solution between two fresh LoBind® tubes (500 μL each).
Add DMSO (5 μL) to one tube.
Add 10 mM DDD01510706 DMSO stock (5 μL; final concentration of 0.1 mM) to the second tube.
Incubate both tubes for 30 minutes at 4°C with rotation.
Transfer blank bead-treated lysate samples to tubes containing pre-washed drug beads.
Incubate at 4°C with rotation for 1 hour.
Centrifuge at 10,000 g for 30 seconds at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant.
Wash twice with 0.5 mL ice-cold wash buffer.
Wash twice with 0.5 mL ice-cold TBS.
Add 25 μL NuPAGE buffer to the samples.
Heat at 95°C in a heat block for 10 minutes.
Incubate samples at room temperature for 5 minutes after removal from the heat block.
Load samples onto a 4–12% NuPAGE Bis-Tris gel, leaving two empty lanes between each sample.
Electrophorese the gel at 150 V for 10 minutes in NuPAGE 1×MOPS SDS Running Buffer.
Submerge the gel in Coomassie Quick Reagent with gentle agitation using a benchtop orbital shaker or equivalent for 60 minutes.
Aspirate the Coomassie reagent and rinse the gel gently with ddH2O.
Cut out each lane using a scalpel blade.
Transfer gel slices to labeled LoBind® tubes.
Transfer the gel band into a 1.5 mL tube using clean tweezers.
Cut the gel pieces into small pieces using a scalpel.
Wash the gel pieces with 200 μL water (milliQ) at room temperature with agitation for 15 min.
Centrifuge the samples at 3,000 g for 1 min and remove washing solution.
Wash the gel pieces with 200 μL acetonitrile at room temperature with agitation for 15 min.
Centrifuge the samples at 3,000 g for 1 min and remove washing solution.
Wash the gel pieces with 200 μL 100 mM tetraethylammonium bicarbonate pH 8.5 (TEAB) at room temperature with agitation for 15 min.
Centrifuge the samples at 3,000 g for 1 min and remove washing solution.
Wash the gel pieces with 200 μL 50% acetonitrile in 100 mM TEAB at room temperature with agitation for 15 min.
Centrifuge the samples at 3,000 g for 1 min and remove washing solution.
Wash the gel pieces with 100 μL acetonitrile at room temperature with agitation for 10 min.
Centrifuge the samples at 3,000 g for 1 min and remove washing solution.
Vacuum dry the samples in an evaporator for 10 min at 30°C using a program suitable for water-based samples.
Add 50 μL of 10 mM dithiothreitol in 100 mM TEAB or enough volume to cover the gel, whichever is greater.
Incubate for 60 min at 56°C.
Centrifuge at 3,000 g for 1 min.
Remove all liquid from the samples and let them equilibrate to room temperature (22°C) for 5 min.
Add 50 μL of 50 mM iodoacetamide in 100 mM TEAB or enough volume to cover the gel, whichever is greater.
Incubate for 30 min at room temperature.
Centrifuge at 3,000 g for 1 min.
Remove all liquid from the samples.
Wash the gel pieces with 200 μL of 100 mM TEAB at room temperature with agitation (600 rpm) for 15 min.
Centrifuge at 3,000 g for 1 min and remove washing solution.
Wash the gel pieces with 200 μL of 50% acetonitrile in 100 mM TEAB at room temperature with agitation (600 rpm) for 15 min.
Centrifuge at 3,000 g for 1 min and remove washing solution.
Wash the gel pieces with 100 μL of acetonitrile at room temperature with agitation (600 rpm) for 10 min.
Centrifuge at 3,000 g for 1 min and remove washing solution.
Vacuum dry the samples in an evaporator for 10 min at 30°C using a program suitable for water-based samples.
Add 10 μL of 12.5 mg/mL trypsin in 100 mM TEAB to cover gel pieces with a protein:enzyme ratio of approximately 25:1.
Incubate the mixture for 30 minutes at room temperature with agitation (600 rpm) to allow rehydration of the gel pieces.
Incubate samples for over 16 hours at 30°C with agitation (600 rpm).
Add one volume of acetonitrile and incubate at 30°C for 15 minutes with agitation (600 rpm).
Transfer the liquid from tube 1 to a new tube (tube 2) containing the peptides.
Add one volume of 5% aqueous formic acid to tube 1 with the gel pieces and incubate at 30°C with agitation (600 rpm) for 15 minutes.
Add one volume of acetonitrile to tube 1 with the gel pieces and incubate at 30°C with agitation (600 rpm) for 45 minutes.
Transfer all liquid from this step to tube 2 containing the peptides.
Vacuum dry tube 1 in an evaporator at 30°C using a program suitable for water-based samples.
Add 10 μL of acetonitrile to the gel pieces in tube 1 and incubate at 30°C for 15 minutes with agitation (600 rpm).
Transfer all liquid from this step to tube 2 containing peptides.
Discard tube 1.
Vacuum dry the peptide samples in an evaporator overnight (8-16 hours) at 30°C using a program suitable for water-based samples.
Resuspend samples in 100 μL of 100 mM TEAB solution.
Pipette a 1 μL aliquot from the resuspended sample.
Dilute the 1 μL aliquot 1:5 in 0.1% (v/v) aqueous formic acid.
Load 5 μL of diluted sample onto a trap column pre-equilibrated with Buffer C at 10 μL/min.
Wash the trap column with Buffer C for 3 min at 10 μL/min.
Switch the trap column in line with the resolving column.
Elute peptides from the resolving column at a constant flow rate of 700 nL/min using a linear gradient from 2% to 40% Buffer D over 7 min, then from 40% to 98% Buffer D over 1 min.
Wash the column with 98% Buffer D for 1 min and re-equilibrate in 2% Buffer D for 5 min.
Acquire MS1 scan cycles with a mass-to-charge ratio (m/z) range of 335–1,800, maximum ion injection time of 30 ms, resolution of 70,000, and automatic gain control (AGC) value of 1 × 10^6.
Perform 10 sequential dependent MS2 scans with an isolation window set to 1.4 m/z, a resolution at 17,500, maximum ion injection time at 100 ms, and AGC of 2 × 10^5.
Open .raw files using Thermo Xcalibur™ (Qual browser).
Select peaks on the upper chromatogram window.
Display relative abundance and m/z of selected peak in the lower window.
Check that most peaks have a charge lower than 4 (z < 4).
Remove 1×TMT 10plex sachet from storage at −20°C.
Allow TMT 10plex sachet to equilibrate to room temperature.
Resuspend dried peptide samples in 100 mM TEAB (100 μL).
Incubate resuspended samples with agitation (600 rpm) at room temperature.
Check that the pH of samples is ≥ 8.
Add 41 μL of acetonitrile to each TMT tube.
Incubate TMT tubes with agitation (600 rpm) for 5 min at room temperature.
Briefly centrifuge peptide samples and TMT tubes (3,000 g, 10 s).
Add the content of each TMT tube to the corresponding peptide sample.
Incubate combined samples with agitation for 1 h at room temperature.
Dilute the quenching reagent to a final concentration of 5% hydroxylamine solution by adding it to 100 mM TEAB in a 10-fold dilution ratio.
Incubate at 37°C until the precipitated quenching reagent clears, if present.
Add 8 μL of the 5% hydroxylamine solution to each reaction tube and incubate with agitation for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Centrifuge each reaction tube at 3,000 g for 10 seconds at room temperature.
Combine the treated samples from ten reactions in a single LoBind® 2 mL tube.
Combine the control samples from ten reactions in another LoBind® 2 mL tube.
Vacuum dry the pooled samples overnight (8–16 hours) at 30°C using an evaporator set to program “HPLC” for water and organic solvent-based samples.
Resuspend the dried pooled samples in 0.1% aqueous TFA solution (300 μL).
Place desalting columns into LoBind® tubes and centrifuge at 5,000 g for 1 minute to remove equilibration buffer.
Discard flow-through after each wash step during column processing.
Wash the desalting columns twice with 100% ACN (300 μL) followed by discarding the flow-through after washing.
Wash the desalting columns a further two times with 0.1% aqueous TFA solution (300 μL), then discard the flow-through.
Add samples to separate desalting columns.
Centrifuge at 3,000 g for 1 minute at room temperature.
Discard the flow-through.
Wash columns three times with 0.1% (v/v) aqueous TFA.
Centrifuge at 3,000 g for 1 minute at room temperature.
Discard the flow-through after each wash.
Wash columns twice with 5% methanol diluted in 0.1% aqueous TFA.
Centrifuge at 3,000 g for 1 minute at room temperature.
Elute peptides from desalting columns using 50% ACN in 0.1% aqueous TFA.
Collect eluates in fresh 2 mL LoBind® tubes.
Repeat the elution process twice with 300 μL of elution solution each time.
Vacuum dry the desalted eluates using program “Aqueous” in the recommended evaporator.
Turn on UV lamp at wavelength 220 nm at least 15 minutes prior to a run.
Purge the system with Buffer A (10 mM ammonium formate, pH 9.5).
Purge the system with Buffer B (10 mM ammonium formate in 90% ACN, pH 9.5).
Set buffer composition to 98% A:2% B.
Set flow rate to 0.2 mL min−1.
Prime the syringe and wash the needle and fluidics using the commands in the Chromeleon software.
Run the HPLC for 15 minutes to fully equilibrate the system.
Prepare a standard containing caffeine and MRFA by diluting 2 μL of each solution (1 mg/mL) in 100 μL buffer A.
Place the sample tube with the prepared standard in the samples tray.
Load 25 μL of the standard sample onto the column.
Elute peptides from the column with a gradient of 2–20% Buffer B over 8 minutes.
Increase the percentage of Buffer B to 47% over the next 37 minutes.
Wash the column with 100% Buffer B for 15 minutes.
Collect fractions from 1 to 80 minutes of the run and discard them.
Check the chromatogram for two peaks at minutes 12 and 14 corresponding to caffeine and MRFA, respectively.
Resuspend the dry sample in 200 μL buffer A.
Vortex the resuspended sample vigorously.
Spin down the sample at 20,000 g at 4°C for 15 minutes.
Transfer 190 μL of supernatant to a new sample tube.
Adjust the pH of the transferred solution to >9 using aqueous ammonia.
Place the transfer tube in the sample tray.
Label 80 collection tubes and add 20 μL of 10% (v/v) aqueous FA to neutralize pH.
Place the labeled collection tubes in the collection trays.
Run the sample using the specified program, loading 185 μL of sample.
Combine fractions from minutes 3–63 into 10 fractions by concatenating them.
Discard fractions from minutes 1 and 2 due to TMT-related contaminants.
Discard fractions from minute 64 onwards as they may contain detergent and further contaminants.
Repeat the run with a standard, intercalating standard runs.
Vacuum dry the concatenated fractions using program “Aqueous” in the recommended evaporator.
Store concatenated fractions at −20°C for up to 6 months if needed.
Calibrate the mass spectrometer prior to analysis of samples.
Resuspend the concatenated samples in 50 μL of 1% aqueous FA.
Load 5 μL aliquots (at 15 μL min−1) onto the trap column previously equilibrated with buffers C and D.
Wash the column for 5 minutes with 5% Buffer D at 15 μL min−1.
Connect the trap column to the resolving column.
Elute peptides at 300 nL min−1 with a linear gradient starting at 10% Buffer D for 1 minute, increasing to 18% at 89 minutes, then to 27% at 134 minutes, and up to 90% Buffer D at 139 minutes.
Wash the column with 90% Buffer D for 10 min.
Re-equilibrate the column in 10% Buffer D for 25 min.
Use Orbitrap Eclipse in data-dependent mode.
Perform MS1 scan cycles from m/z range 380–1,500 at resolution of 120,000 with standard automatic gain control (AGC).
Conduct 15 sequential dependent MS2 scans with an isolation window set to 0.7 Da and maximum ion injection time at 50 ms.
Perform MS3 scans with a resolution of 50,000, an isolation window set to 0.7 Da, and maximum injection time at 120 ms.
Activate the real-time search feature using the P. falciparum 3D7 annotated proteins FASTA file (downloaded from PlasmoDB, latest version).
Download the P. falciparum 3D7 annotated proteins FASTA file from PlasmoDB.org.
Download the human proteome FASTA from Uniprot with accession number 9606.
Set up the experiment in MaxQuant by loading RAW files and labeling them according to their condition and replicate using the “Set experiment” button.
Select the fraction number for each sample using the “Set fraction” button, typing numbers 1 through 10.
In Group-specific parameters, set Reporter ion MS3 under Type and choose the 10plex TMT option.
Adjust the correction factors in the table according to the Reporter ion isotopic distributions table in the TMT10plex product data sheet.
Choose Oxidation (M), Acetyl (Protein N-term), Dioxidation (W), Deamidation (NW) and Gln->Pyro-Glu as variable modifications.
Select Carbamidomethyl (C) as a fixed modification under Modifications.
Select Trypsin/P enzyme under “Digestion”.
Add the FASTA files containing the protein sequences in the “Sequences” tab.
Set FTMS MS/MS Match tolerance to 10 ppm and ITMS MS/MS Match tolerance to 0.5 Da in the “MS/MS analyzer” tab.
Activate the “Match between runs” option in the “Identification” tab.
Open Perseus software (version 1.6.15.0).
Load the proteinGroups.txt file from the analysis folder\combined\txt using the “Generic matrix upload” button.
Select the “Reporter intensity corrected” columns 1–10 and add them to the “Main” box by clicking the “>” button.
Click “Ok”.
Click on the “Filter rows” tab and select the option “Filter rows based on categorical columns”.
Select “Only identified by site” and click on “OK”.
Open the “Scatter plot” tab.
Choose the “log2 fold-change” column in the “X” tab.
Select the “Lin” option next to the “X” tab.
Choose the “Intensity” column in the “Y” tab.
Select the “Log” option next to the “Y” tab.
Identify non-enriched proteins that populate the zero line on the X-axis.
Treat proteins with log2 fold-change values less than 2 and negative values as noise.
Consider hits with log2 fold-change value greater than 2 in two independent experiments as putative hits.
Remove proteins identified with less than 2 unique peptides from analysis.
Regard proteins with 2 or 3 unique peptides with caution.
Use Perseus statistical tools to find significantly enriched proteins optionally.
